Header: Ceratitis cosyra, C. capitata, Bactrocera invadens

Prevention: Synchronize planting timing with other farmers in the area
Avoid planting pepper near alternate hosts (mango, citrus, watermelons, tomatoes, eggplants, avocado) to reduce pest populations
Remove non-harvested pepper and wild melon and pumpkins as they will host larvae.
Till the field top soil (5 to 10cm deep) before planting to expose pupae to the sun, birds, poultry and parasites.
Conserve natural enemies like ants, rove beetles, birds and parasitic wasps by practising mixed/ intercropping to enhance biodiversity, and avoid the use of broad spectrum insecticides
Monitoring: Start monitoring as soon as fruits begin to develop.
Inspect plants weekly to look for brownish or yellowish wasp-like flies on plants
Look for signs of infestation which include dot-like scars, fruit flies laying their eggs inside the skin of the fruit and larvae (maggots) feeding inside the fruit.
Check for rotten and fallen fruit.
Look for adult flies on the plants.
Use food baits e.g. waste brewers’ yeast 45ml/L of water or ripe fruits as bait to monitor presence of fruit flies.
For early detection, use commercial pheromone traps with trimedlure, cue lure, or methyl eugenol (3 traps/ 50m 2 )
Take action when 2-5 adult fruit flies are observed per 5m 2 plants in the plantation
Direct Control: Collect dropped fruits and bury them outside the field at a depth of 60+ cm with plastic bags
Trap fruit flies using pheromone traps - Methyl
Cera lure/ Capilure impregnated with an insecticide such as deltamethrin as killing agent (see yellow control), at 1 trap per 30m plot.
GF120-food bait with 10 ml trimed lure or methyl eugenol + 1ml insecticide filled into plastic bottles with holes, or into commercial traps.
Use 3 to 5 traps across a field per 1 acre
The spray should contain ½ cup (150 ml) of the bait mixed with 5L water.
Methyl eugenol 1 septa per trap, with 1ml
Malathion (see yellow control) on a cotton ball.
Use 6 traps/ropani, evenly spaced, and use them at the time of flowering and just before fruit set
Restrictions: When using a pesticide or botanical, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label.
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance, always consult the most recent list of registered pesticides of
Insecticides used as killing agents in pheromone traps or added to baits
Pyrethroid insecticide with contact and residual activity
